newsitem.title: USA: Nutrition For Life says wins court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Nutrition For Life says wins court ruling.

text.p: Nutrition For Life International Inc said Friday it has been awarded a default judgment in its lawsuit against a former major shareholder of a predecessor of the company for statements made on the Internet.
The level of actual and punitive damages and other relief has not yet been decided, the company said.
The company had sued Greg Caton for libel, slander, defamation and breach of contract for statements he allegedly made on the Internet and elsewhere.
In a similar suit against Caton that was filed by Kevin Trudeau, a distributor of the company, $10 million in damages was awarded, the company said.

Nutrition For Life said the court issued an order barring Caton and any other individual or entity acting on his behalf from publishing any of the allegedly defamatory statements called into question by the lawsuit. Those statements include allegations against Trudeau and the company that its advertising campaign is fraudulent and deceptive, it said.
Caton was described by the company as a former major shareholder of its predecessor. It said he disassociated with that firm in 1987.
Nutrition For Life develops, markets and sells nutritional supplements and other consumer products.
Nutrition For Life's lawsuit against Caton was filed in the 61st Judicial District of Harris County in Texas. Caton could not be reached for comment.
